_comment: Shared vectors for the D-221 uninstall-token derivation. Read by
as lowercase hex, where window = floor(unix_seconds / 300) * 300. 'bound' entries pin it.
'legacy_express' and 'legacy_worker' entries pin the two PREVIOUS derivations, which
Q2-A keeps verifying for one release: Express used HMAC(secret, str(window)) and the
Worker used SHA256('<window>:<secret>'). They are different on purpose — that divergence
is the defect D-221 records, and these vectors are how it stops being invisible.
The secret is a fixed test value so the vectors are reproducible; it is not a real token.
legacy_sunset_reason: The previous deployment-wide derivation is still accepted (ruling Q2-A) so a device whose agent has not taken the update can uninstall. That acceptance must end, and a tag-driven repo has no release cadence for 'one release' to point at, so it ends on a date: 90 days from the D-221 close. scripts/test_cross_surface_contract.py FAILS on or after legacy_sunset and names the deletion sites; server/tests/uninstallAuth.test.js and serverless/worker.test.ts fail on the same date, so three suites have to be dealt with rather than one log line ignored. To close it out: delete legacyUninstallToken() and legacyUninstallToken() (Worker) plus their verify branches and the deprecated_scheme marker, drop the two legacy tests, then empty legacy_express and legacy_worker here (the vectors that prove the two schemes differed become history in the D-221 ledger entry).
